### Makegood triggers and breach handling gaps
- **Status:** active
- **Summary:** A member identified gaps in how makegoods work today: the existing triggers (breached performance-standard thresholds, billing variance beyond the allowed percentage) miss common cases such as wrong-geo delivery, where impression counts match and no billing variance arises. A broadcast-side member agreed that matching counts does not establish targeting compliance and suggested the protocol let parties identify affected delivery, reference the contractual requirement, and record the resolution. They also argued that over-delivery should distinguish delivered volume from billable volume with disputed charges identified, and that breach detection and notification is partly a platform concern, with the protocol carrying notifications and evidence references.
- **Thread:** https://agenticads.slack.com/archives/C09BK148CLU/p1794914494367739, https://agenticads.slack.com/archives/C0ACHCU5210/p1794934174429839

### Versioning rules and cross-release translation
- **Status:** active
- **Summary:** A proposal to make cross-release translation in SDKs normative drew an objection on all three of its items, with an alternative offered. A concession now proposes adopting three versioning rules for the rest of 3.x and all of 4.x, starting with the principle that a minor release only adds, and only to open schemas. The group was asked to confirm this approach as a decision item.
- **Related:** #8519, #8704
- **Thread:** https://agenticads.slack.com/archives/C09BK148CLU/p1793989289197729

### Beta SDK version-pin handling on capability discovery
- **Status:** active
- **Summary:** An implementer reported that a reader built on the 3.3 beta SDK pinned a prerelease version when calling capability discovery against a seller supporting 3.0, received a version-unsupported error, and did not retry unpinned, causing registration checks to fail. Per the 3.3 beta guidance, prerelease pins should only go to peers advertising that exact value and never negotiate down, so on that error the buyer should retry without the pin; the stable SDK does this. The thread also notes that capability discovery is expected to be readable without credentials, so sellers locking down auth should account for anonymous probes.
- **Thread:** https://agenticads.slack.com/archives/C09J28K9K29/p1794418915773829

### Agent registry openness, trust signals, and lookup
- **Status:** active
- **Summary:** A set of proposals aims to make the agent registry more useful: allow anyone to be listed with owner-controlled visibility (pending an executive committee decision), add an environment tag and dated evidence badges (authorized, reachable, conformant, observed) with basic listing checks, and add identity lookup, a public MCP server, and capability-based search. Two items, the environment tag and public readability, can proceed without waiting on the broader decision.
- **Related:** #9067, #9058, #9059
- **Thread:** https://agenticads.slack.com/archives/C09PK59GUCB/p1794868197220489

### Synthetic population-model alternative to ID-based matching
- **Status:** parked
- **Summary:** A member proposed evaluating a fully synthetic approach in which the buy side plans reach and frequency on a large population model and passes virtual IDs to the sell side, which maps its audiences to them, avoiding match-rate and consent-state problems. A follow-up agreed this would suit a dedicated working group, but no spec work has started.
